Issue_Reported: Expired Immunology tubes required the use of alternate tubes for combined blood draw.
Description_of_Action_Taken: Nursing reported lack of tubes for combined blood draw. A work around was implemented. Blood volume was nominal. Principal Investigator (PI) was satisfied with preservation of conditions and blood volume and expects no impact to science. Coordinator on Duty (COD) worked with UTMB clinical and research labs, ER, GCRC and FARU to determine if other tubes could be found of the prescribed variety and to seek alternatives. FAP Study Lead and subsequently the Ops Lead informed. In the place of the 3 ml Li Heparin tubes, one 2 ml Li Heparin and two 0.5 ml Li Heparin tubes were used. The prescribed volume and conditions were maintained. The small tubes were microtainers. Microtainers do not have a vacuum by which to draw. To prevent risk of cross contamination by additives, the samples for these tubes were drawn by syringe at the end of the draw after removal of the vacutainer needle from the butterfly. Nutrition test operators were updated on tube work around for transport.
Disposition_Comments: Blood draw was salvaged with no science impact. Spare tubes are maintained on the FARU for use in such cases. Tubes are inventoried weekly for supply and expiration dates.
